correctness.rationale: Exact proof uses a 10-facet nerve justified by a good cover. For all 988 fault subsets with |F|<=3, 2,632 supplied elementary free-face pairs are verified by an exhaustive all-coface test; residues are connected graphs or void. Integral homotopy types follow from simplicial collapses and nerve theorem, with independent direct-face Euler crosschecks and two independent perfect-matching enumerations.

originality.rationale: The complete homotopy atlas for 1, 2 and 3 deleted edges and its multiplicity table are not consequences of the published intact Dürer perfect-matching collapsibility or equivariant contractibility: a subcomplex obtained by removing facets may have arbitrary changed homotopy. The Dürer ordinary matching complex additionally includes nonextendible matchings, and the two primary papers study different graph families. Actual semantic searches found no direct covering theorem. Priority against unindexed equivalences is a residual risk.

value.rationale: A natural complete cubic-graph fault-tolerance atlas through the minimum-degree threshold of three, not a chosen arbitrary slice. It identifies three distinct one-edge orbit responses, the complete two-edge response, and a sharp three-edge transition including precisely twenty void cases, loss of the rank-two class, and two exceptional alternating-rim rank-three cases. Intact contractibility cannot predict these changes.
